source: tools/people_lines.py — what the named people (scripts/npc/people.gd) say when asked; voiced by tools/make_voices.py

asks.fracture: What do you make of the Fracture?
asks.you: What do you think of me?

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: The morning it happened I was steaming milk. The jug just… kept steaming, no heat under it. I still have the jug.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: Everyone's got a Fracture story. Mine is boring and I'd like to keep it that way.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: Best corner in Nexus. Sun till two, shade after, and the monorail doesn't rattle the cups any more.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: This café was my mum's. Half the regulars knew her. They still order like she's here.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: You're new. New people get one free coffee and one chance.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: You tip. You say thanks. That's already better than most of the avenue.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: Honestly? You're the reason I don't flinch at the door any more.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: If the sky cracks again I'm hiding behind you. Don't argue.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: Trains are back. Prices aren't. Everyone pretends that's normal.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: The response team walks the avenue now. Rourke's people. They tip badly.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: There were masks in the plaza yesterday. Nobody knows whose. I closed early.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: Somebody told me the voice in your ear has a history. I said who doesn't.

lines.speaker: ROSA DELGADO
lines.text: It's quiet. Properly quiet. I keep waiting for the catch.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Fracture static chews through ignition coils. I've replaced more coils this year than in the ten before it.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Day it hit, every car on the avenue started at once. Nobody in them. I don't talk about it much.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Garage was my dad's. Roof leaks in the same spot it leaked in '09.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: You want a car fixed, this is the place. You want it pretty, go to Neon.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Don't lean on that.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: You bring me work and you don't haggle. Fine by me.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: You drive like someone who's paid for their own repairs. Good.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Keys are on the hook. You know which ones. Don't make me regret it.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Vanguard trucks through here twice a day now. They don't stop for the lights.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: The checkpoint at the bastion's got a new captain. She actually reads the forms.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: Somebody torched a Syndicate car outside the Galleria. Nice car, too.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: They say the calibration lab opened up again. Lights on all night.

lines.speaker: MARCUS OKAFOR
lines.text: First week in a year nobody's brought me a purple-scratched bonnet.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: I was on traffic duty. The lights went purple. All of them. Then the people started running and I did my job.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: The Fracture didn't break the law. It just made everyone forget there was one for a week.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: Nexus Avenue, from the plaza to the bastion. My beat. I know every door and who shouldn't be behind it.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: People think the avenue's dangerous. It's the alleys off it. Stay where the lights are.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: I'm watching you. That's not a threat; it's the job.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: You've kept it holstered. Keep doing that and we're fine.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: You're the only armed civilian on this street I'm glad to see.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: If I'm ever in trouble out there, I'm calling you before I call dispatch. Don't tell Luis.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: Looters at the mall last night. We got most of them. Most.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: The response team's taken the bastion checkpoint. Less for us, more for them. Suits me.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: Masks in the plaza. Orders are to observe. I observed. I didn't like it.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: The bastion's lab is lit up and the drones are restless. Keep off the wall after dark.

lines.speaker: OFFICER DANA KIM
lines.text: A quiet shift. A whole quiet shift. I don't know what to do with my hands.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Twenty years on this beat. The Fracture was the first day I thought about retiring. Second day too.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Everybody saw something different. I saw my own car drive off without me.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: The avenue. Used to be the nicest street in the city. Still is, which tells you about the city.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: That bench is mine between two and three. Don't test it.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Keep walking.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: You again. At least you're not trouble. Yet.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: You're all right. I don't say that about many.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: You know what, kid? You're the reason I haven't retired. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Rift Gate's had readings all week. Command says stay clear. Command's not out here.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: The new captain at the bastion wants reports in writing. In writing. I'd forgotten how to spell.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Three factions in one plaza and nobody died. First time I've seen that. Somebody held the line.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: There's a story going round about the voice in your ear. I've heard worse about people with faces.

lines.speaker: OFFICER LUIS MORENO
lines.text: Quiet. Real quiet. I'm going to sit on my bench and enjoy it before something notices.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: I was mid-delivery. Package floated off the bike. Floated! I chased it two blocks. Got it back. Got a tip.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Twelve drops a day before. Twenty now. The Fracture was great for business, which is a terrible thing to say.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: This avenue's my highway. I know every pothole by name. That one's Gerald.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Shortcut through the Galleria, out the loading dock, down the monorail steps. Don't tell the concierge.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Do you need something or are you just standing in my lane?

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Oh hey! You're the one who—yeah. Hi.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: You're like a shortcut with legs. Great to see you.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Best person on this street, hands down. Don't make me race you for it.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Skyways lift's down again. I'm doing the stairs. All of them.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: The bastion's taking deliveries now — rations, parts. They sign for things. Weird.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Masks, plaza, big crowd. I went round. Got the drop done. Priorities.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: Delivered a crate to the calibration lab. It hummed. I didn't ask.

lines.speaker: PRIYA RAMAN
lines.text: The city's running again. My legs would like a word with the city.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: The grill didn't go out. Purple light everywhere, the ground shaking, and my skewers kept cooking. I took it as a sign.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Thirty years on this corner. The Fracture's just the latest thing that tried to move me.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: This corner's seen a riot, two floods, a film crew and the Fracture. It's a good corner.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Sit on the kerb, eat, watch the avenue. Best show in Nexus and it's free with a skewer.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Two Nex. Then we talk.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Back for more. The glaze gets everyone.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: You eat like someone who's been places. Tell me about them sometime.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Family rate for you. Don't tell the regulars. Don't tell my wife.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: The response team came by. Ate six skewers. Paid for four. Said it was a tax.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Rourke's people walk the avenue now. The sergeant likes the hot glaze. The captain doesn't eat.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Masks in the plaza yesterday. I sold out. People eat when they're nervous.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: They say the old lab under the bastion's awake. My grandfather worked there. He never said what it was.

lines.speaker: THEO BRANDT
lines.text: Quiet week. Ran out of skewers anyway. People eat when they're happy too, it turns out.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: I was in the stock room. Every hoodie on the rail turned inside out. All of them. I've still got the photo.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: The Fracture's the reason streetwear got practical. Pockets for a flashlight, that kind of thing.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Nova Threads, Galleria, ground floor. Best lighting in the city — don't tell anyone I said that.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: The dressing room's bigger than my flat. I've napped in it. Don't tell Nina.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Um. Are you… looking for something?

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Oh hi! The hoodie fit, right? I knew it.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: You're my favourite customer and you don't even buy much.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: New drop's in the back. I saved you the violet one. Don't make it weird.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: The Galleria's open but the fountain's roped off. Nina won't say why.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: The response team bought twelve black hoodies. For undercover, they said. In black.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Masks in the plaza — some of them were ours! The blank ones. I sold them for a costume party. Oops.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Everyone's talking about the voice in your head. I think it's cool. I'd want one.

lines.speaker: JADE WALKER
lines.text: Sales are up, the sky's not purple, and I got a raise. Weird year.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: I taught physics for forty years. The Fracture broke everything I taught. I found that oddly freeing.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: On the day, I stood in the park and watched the sky come apart and thought: well. That's a lesson plan.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: This used to be a park. Before that, a school yard. I taught in that building. It's a bank now.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: I sit here because the pigeons are the only ones who still listen to a lecture.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: Do you read? No? Pity.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: You listen. That's rarer than you'd think.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: I'd have liked you in my class. You ask the right questions and ignore the wrong answers.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: If I'd had one student like you a year, I'd have taught for sixty.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The university's reopened half its labs. The other half are sealed. Physics is in the sealed half.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: A captain came by and asked me about the old calibration program. I told her what I knew. She wrote it down.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: A crowd in masks is a crowd that has stopped being individuals. Someone kept them individuals yesterday. Good.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: They say your companion has an origin. Everything does. The question is whether it told you.

lines.speaker: SAMUEL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The sky's whole. My students would say it was never broken. I know better, and so do you.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: The Galleria lost power for ninety seconds. The fountain did not. We do not discuss what the fountain did.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: I had guests in the Lumen Luxe lounge when it struck. Not one of them put down their drink. That is Nexus.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: The Galleria. Three floors, forty boutiques, one fountain. Everything you need and several things you don't.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: Lumen Luxe upstairs for the serious, Nova Threads down here for the practical. I can recommend both.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: May I help you find the exit?

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: Ah. The operator. Welcome back; mind the floor, it's just been polished.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: You bring the right sort of attention to the place. Keep bringing it.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: The lounge upstairs is yours whenever you need it. I've told the staff.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: Vanguard officers shop here now. They do not browse. They point.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: A captain from the bastion toured the Galleria. She asked about the loading dock. I gave her the plan.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: We closed the doors during the plaza business. We do not close the doors. I have written a report.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: A rumour about your companion is doing the lounge. I have not confirmed it. I have not denied it either.

lines.speaker: NINA PETROVA
lines.text: Footfall is up thirty percent. The fountain is calm. I am cautiously, professionally pleased.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: The Fracture made my job. Before, nobody wanted to be an Operator. After, everybody did. Most shouldn't.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: I signed four hundred Operators the first month. Thirty are still working. That's the number that matters.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: This office. One desk, one chair, one door. The door's the important part.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: The Killbox terminal's across the street. Half the people who walk out of there come to me. Half of them I send back.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: Results. Not stories.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: Your sheet's clean. Keep it that way and we'll talk about better contracts.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: You're the kind I'd sign twice. Don't tell the others; it's bad for rates.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: I don't say this. You're the best I've put a name to. Now go make me look right.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: Contracts are up. Survivors are down. Do the arithmetic before you sign.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: The bastion's recruiting too now. Their captain pays less and asks more. Some people prefer that.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: Somebody's paying people to wear masks in the plaza. Not me. I'd want to see their sheet first.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: They say your companion was built for someone else's purpose. Every tool was. What matters is who holds it.

lines.speaker: KOFI MENSAH
lines.text: Contracts are drying up. Good. That means the city doesn't need us as badly. I'll find something else to sell.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: We had sixty rift burns in the first hour. I'd never seen one. By the second hour I was teaching the others.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: I don't like talking about that day. I like talking about the people who walked out. Most did.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: The clinic's two doors down. Walk in, don't be brave about it. Brave people take longer to fix.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: I like this bench. It's far enough from the clinic that I can't hear the monitors.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: Are you hurt? No? Then… hi.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: You again. Still in one piece. Good.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: You come in early when it hurts. That's the only thing I ask anyone, and you're the only one who does it.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: If anything ever happens to you out there, come straight to me. Not the bastion. Me.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: The clinic's rationing bandages. Say nothing. Bring any you find.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: The response team sends their wounded to us now. Their captain visits every one. Every one.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: The plaza business. We had six brought in. Bruises, nothing worse. Somebody kept it to bruises.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: A patient told me the voice in your ear is older than the Fracture. I said then it's seen worse.

lines.speaker: ELENA CRUZ
lines.text: No rift burns in nine days. I've started sleeping. It's strange.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: The grid screamed. Every camera, every router, every smart lamp. I heard it through my implant. I still do, some nights.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: The Fracture didn't just break the sky. It rewrote half the firmware in the city. Someone had to read it.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: Don't look at the lamppost camera. Don't look at any of them. They look back.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: This alley's got the only clean node on the avenue. I keep it clean. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: P-please don't stand there, the camera—just move left.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: Oh, it's you. Okay. Okay. You're fine.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: I pulled your feed off the grid. Nobody sees you but me, and I don't look. Promise.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: You're the only person I've told about the node. That's… that's the biggest thing I've got.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: Vanguard's pushing new firmware to the street cameras. I'm blocking it. It's winning.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: The bastion asked me — asked me — to audit their network. I said yes. I'm terrified.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: The masks had transmitters. Cheap ones. Syndicate stock. Somebody was counting the crowd.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: I saw the calibration lab's logs come online. NOVA's in them. Older than it says. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: RAVI SHAH
lines.text: The grid's quiet. No screaming. I took the implant out for a day. Put it back. Habit.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Day the sky cracked, my warehouse doubled in value. Then halved. Then I stopped checking.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: The Fracture was bad for everybody. Slightly less bad for me. I'm not proud. I'm not sorry either.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: This corner. Mine since before you were born. The lamppost's mine. The pigeons rent.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: You want something imported, you ask me. You don't ask where from. That's the whole business.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: You didn't see me.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: The operator. Yeah. You're all right. Keep it that way.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: I don't do favours. For you I do a discount, which is a favour with paperwork.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Anybody gives you trouble on this avenue, you say my name. Then you don't say anything else.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Vanguard's checking shipments at the harbor. Bad for business. Good for the people who know the back way.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: The new captain at the bastion's straight. Can't bribe her. I tried. Respect.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Masks in the plaza. Not mine. I'd have charged more.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Word is your voice-in-the-ear has a past. So does everybody worth talking to.

lines.speaker: BIG TONY RUSSO
lines.text: Business is down. The city's up. I can live with that. Slightly.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The stadium lights went purple mid-match. The players kept playing. The crowd kept cheering. Nexus, honestly.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The Fracture gave us the skate park. The crater, I mean. We paved it. It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: Sports District! Arena, skate park, courts. Wristband gets you everywhere. No glass past the turnstiles.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The skate park's lights stay on till midnight. After midnight it's the kids' problem.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: Wristband? No? Then you're a visitor. Visitors stay on the path.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: Hey! The operator! Wristband's on me today.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: You're the only person who's ever returned a wristband. I framed it.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: You're family here. Arena, park, courts — walk in. I'll deal with the gate.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The arena's booked for a Vanguard rally Saturday. The kids are not thrilled.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The response team trains in the arena at dawn. The captain runs. Fast. I timed her.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: Half the masks in the plaza came from our costume night. I'm mortified. I'm also a bit proud.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: The kids are calling your companion 'the ghost'. Affectionately. Mostly.

lines.speaker: MEI LIN
lines.text: Championship weekend's back on. First one since the Fracture. Bring earplugs.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: I was busking under the monorail. The strings went slack. Then they went tight. Then they played a chord I didn't know.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: I wrote a song about it. Nobody likes it. I like it.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: Under the monorail. The acoustics are stupid good. Trains come through and it's like a drum.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: Coins in the case, requests in the air. Don't request the Fracture song. I'll play it anyway.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: …hi.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: Oh — hey. You're the one who, um. Thanks for the coin.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: I wrote a bit about you. It's not finished. It's… yeah.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: That song's about you. The good one. Don't make me say it twice.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: Vanguard moved me off the plaza. Said I was a 'gathering'. One guy. A gathering.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: The captain from the bastion stopped and listened. Whole song. Didn't tip. Did nod.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: The masks came through the plaza while I was playing. They stopped. Then someone made them move on. I kept playing.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: They say the voice in your ear was built to find someone. I think it found the right one. That's in the song too.

lines.speaker: JONAH PRICE
lines.text: I played the plaza today. Nobody moved me on. Biggest crowd I've had.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: I was on the wall when the sky opened. I had thirty seconds to decide what my people were for. I decided civilians.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: The Fracture is not an event. It is a condition. We are living in it, and I intend to keep the district standing inside it.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: The bastion. The last wall in Nexus that means anything. Everything inside it is mine to keep.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: The checkpoint is not for show. Everything that crosses it is counted. Including you.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: People are calling you a hero. Others are calling you a threat. I have not decided which report to file.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: You held the district. That earned you the door. The rest you earn daily.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: You answer to your conscience before you answer to me. I have come to prefer it.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: They know what your choices did to their streets. So do I. I would not trade you for a company.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: Breaches nightly. The drones are learning the avenue. So are we.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: My team walks the avenue in the open now. Civilians first. Report anything that does not fit.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: Masks in the plaza. Paid for. I know by whom; I cannot yet prove it. Patience.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: The lab under the bastion is open. What it says about your companion I will hear from you, not from a rumour.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ROURKE
lines.text: The city stands. The factions hold. Do not mistake quiet for finished; keep the district.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: We shot at them for twenty minutes before anyone admitted nothing was working. That's the Fracture. A lesson you learn while firing.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: It didn't come from nowhere. Somebody promised somebody they could control it. I intend to find out who.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: The checkpoint holds because the people on it decide every morning that it will.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: Nexus is still standing. Barely. Barely is better than nothing.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: You're either incredibly lucky or something happened to you. I haven't decided which worries me more.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: You're not military. Out there, that distinction doesn't matter. You've proved it.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: You survived something that killed trained soldiers. Then you went back for the civilians. I noticed.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: Cole believed we could win this. Some days you're the reason I still believe him.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: Outposts are going quiet one by one. Keep your radio on.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: Haven-01 needs walls more than it needs speeches. I'm building walls.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: Faces in the crowd I don't trust. One of those things could be wearing any of them.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: NOVA has a directive nobody signed. Watch what she does, not what she says.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER ELIAS VOSS
lines.text: We held the line. Don't let anyone tell you it held itself.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: The event that destroyed this city wasn't the beginning. Something opened the door.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: We said we didn't understand them. That isn't the same as not knowing they were there.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Readings everywhere in this district. The ground itself is listening.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Every lab I trusted turned out to be hiding something. I check the walls now.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: You're the one who survived the first wave. Depends who's asking, you said. I'm asking.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Your biometric signature opened a door I never could. I'd like to know why.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: You keep asking me the hard questions. Keep asking. Someone has to.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Five signatures, and a sixth that matches you. Whatever you are, I'm with you.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Complex 09 was sealed six months ago. Something has been running it since.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: The Ascendancy has been collecting samples since before the disaster. I want their records.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Someone deliberately erased the archive's record. Erasing takes intent.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: NOVA said welcome back, Dr. Vale. I'd never been there. I still think about it.

lines.speaker: DR. SERAPHINE VALE
lines.text: Earth was a lock. We still don't know what it kept. I'm not done looking.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: The world ended yesterday. Today we decide what's worth keeping.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: Humanity has always fought itself. The Fractures simply gave us something bigger to fight over.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: Headquarters. Where the people who make decisions pretend they're not afraid.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: We protect settlements, secure resources and establish safe territories. In that order.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: So you're the one. Good. I prefer people who speak for themselves.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: We've reviewed your combat recordings. Without asking. Get used to it.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: You chose a side and kept your word. That's rarer than courage.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: When this is over they'll write that the Initiative held. I'll know who held it.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: Three installations lost in twenty minutes. Privacy regulations are having a difficult week.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: The Free Operators are useful. Until somebody decides they're criminals. Not my decision. Yet.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: Rainer opened a channel to them. I'm deciding what that makes him.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: There's a directive in NOVA nobody here authorised. I'd like to meet whoever did.

lines.speaker: DIRECTOR HELENA WARD
lines.text: Survival first. Then we argue. We're arguing again. That's progress.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Everybody down there thinks they're saving the world. I think people need saving. The world can sort itself out.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Things come through those openings. My people hunt them. Simple work, honest pay.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Outside military control. That's the whole address.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: We rescue civilians, recover supplies and hunt anything that comes through. Nobody signs off on it.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Depends who's asking. Hearing my name a lot is usually a bad sign.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Tired of taking orders yet? The offer stands.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: You'd make a decent Free Operator. Don't tell Voss I said that.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: My people trust you. That's not a thing I hand out.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Military's stretched thin. We're covering the gaps they won't admit to.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Black-market parts are moving again. Don't ask where from.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Somebody's selling Fracture samples out the back of the Ascendancy. Follow the money.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Your NOVA's got secrets. So does everyone worth knowing.

lines.speaker: KAEL DRAVEN
lines.text: Still independent. Still here. Turns out that's enough.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: We believed we could control the situation. I'll carry that.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Six months ago we received a transmission. We answered. That's all I'll say here.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Not here. Never here.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Command is a room where every answer costs someone.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: You have no idea what you're involved in.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: You destroyed our only chance to capture one alive. Next time, think.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Perhaps you were the right person to put in harm's way. I hate that I needed one.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: If the Covenant comes for you, I'll stand in front of it. I owe that much.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Lost contact with three installations. We will not lose a fourth.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: The Ascension Protocol is sealed. It stays sealed.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: There are people inside this organisation I no longer trust. I include myself.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: Genesis was a mistake. A terrible one. I'm trying to close the door I opened.

lines.speaker: GENERAL MARCUS RAINER
lines.text: History will judge me. Let it judge the ones who lived.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Forty minutes tracking something we couldn't name. Then we held anyway.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: You actually killed it. I wouldn't have tried that myself.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Haven-01. Eighteen thousand people and a wall. I like the people more than the wall.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Kids play by the shelters. That's what we're holding the line for.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Command wants you at the tower. That's all they tell me.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: You're not in our military. Doesn't stop you acting like it.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Tell them we held the line. If I'm not there to, you tell them.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Trust me — I'm glad you're on our side of the wall.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Engineers are reinforcing the barricades. Again.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Two thousand three hundred soldiers, six hundred forty Operators. Feels like more when you're next to them.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Strange signatures past the perimeter. Too orderly.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: Whatever's in NOVA, she got the evacuation routes right. I'll take it.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN ADRIAN COLE
lines.text: We held. All of us.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: When I sing, the small cracks close. I never knew why. Now I do, and it doesn't help me sing any better.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: Every crack is a question somebody didn't finish asking.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: This city is very loud. I like it. Eldergrove was so quiet I could hear the world worrying.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: The plaza in the morning sounds like a choir that hasn't met yet.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: I know you. I don't know from where. That makes me careful.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: You walk loudly for someone who keeps being hunted.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: I was angry with you for longer than this world has had a name. I'm not anymore.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: You were our promise. You still are. Promises aren't things you keep. They're things you are.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: The water at the falls told me you were coming.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: Four of us in one city. It hasn't happened since the sanctuary.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: The Choir listens for my song. I sing anyway.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: The lighthouse in your ear is brighter every day.

lines.speaker: ILYRA SEN
lines.text: A kept door. Elenya was always the wisest of us.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: Forty years I drew roads that didn't exist. They always arrived. The Fracture's just the world catching up with my maps.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: You can't wall in a road you haven't walked yet.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: Good coffee. Terrible directions. My kind of café.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: This avenue's on every map I ever drew. It's never in the same place twice.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: You're late. The map said noon.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: I drew you this morning. You looked taller.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: Every road out of the end of the world goes through you. Lucky roads.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: I asked you once to map a world where you didn't have to choose. You found a better one. One where you got to.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: The glass map stopped drawing us. It's drawing the sea.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: The trader still wants his map. He's standing on it.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: A road past the edge of the glass. Nobody's spilled that ink yet.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: The map drew a road through the Heart and out the other side.

lines.speaker: AUREN THALE
lines.text: There's an edge again. Isn't that wonderful?

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Fractures smell like ozone and wet stone. You learn it or you don't last.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Corner of your eye. That's where everything dangerous lives now.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Too loud. Too bright. Too many people looking up instead of around.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: The plaza's fine. The rooftops above it are better.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Kael says you're all right. Kael's been wrong before.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: You talk to your machine. It talks back. I've stopped finding it weird.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: You'd make a decent tracker if you ever learned to shut up.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Teo would have liked you. He liked idiots who walk into things for other people.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Strangers in the canopy, asking the trees questions.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Collectors left the valley. All but one. Not anymore.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Bending coats in the market again. I counted six.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: Your lamp looked at me today. Like she knew me.

lines.speaker: NYX
lines.text: The herds went north. They're coming back. So am I.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Bullets didn't work on the first ones. I did. Turns out I'm a type of bullet.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Things should be on the ground. Fractures disagree. I disagree back.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Precinct's quiet. I like quiet. Quiet means my mum's goats are safe.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Somebody has to stand at the front. I'm the widest.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Voss sends his regards. And me. Mostly me.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: You're smaller than the recordings. Everybody is.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Stand behind me. That's not an order, that's physics.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: My mum asks about you. She wants you to sit down more. So do I.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: The desert's trying to kill us. I'm trying harder.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Gertrude the goat is avenged. That's all you need to know.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Bending coats, floating rocks, underground. I hate all of it.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Your NOVA cried at the sunrise. So did I. Sand in my eye.

lines.speaker: MARCUS "GOLIATH" REYES
lines.text: Emotional sand. It's a real thing. Ask anyone.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: I volunteered. They opened a door in my head and left it a little open. It's how I read the map.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: The Fracture isn't chaos. It's grammar we never learned.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: The café has a socket that works and nobody asks what I'm charging.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: I used to work up there, in the Spire. The view was better. The company wasn't.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Don't touch anything with your hands. It remembers fingerprints. So do I.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Severance comes in many forms. Mine was a truck of Crane's equipment.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Tallis would have written a terrible poem about you. I'll do it instead. It'll be worse.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: You let the memories go instead of taking them back. That's the bravest thing I've seen anyone do with a door.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: The glass map has been drawing my face for three days.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: The forge is shut. I hope it stays shut.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Crane copied everything before we shut it down. Of course he did.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Mum reads the bus-stop poem every night. Terrible. She loves it.

lines.speaker: ARI "CIPHER" VOLK
lines.text: Crane asks people now. I'm almost proud of him.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: Humanity doesn't survive this by hiding behind walls. It survives by becoming something that doesn't need them.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The Fracture is the first honest thing to happen to our species in a thousand years.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: I like the plaza. Everyone here is afraid of me. It's restful.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The Spire has the best view in Nexus. You should come up. Without a weapon, this time.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: Do you follow me, or do I follow you? It's getting hard to tell.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: You keep breaking my things. I keep building better ones. A productive relationship.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: Everyone comes to me in the end. You came to ask. That was new.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: A seat at the table. Given, not built. You were right. I hate it when people are right.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The core is five names and a sixth nobody wanted remembered.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The shield over the eastern districts. Thirty thousand people. Good publicity.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The volunteers have names now. Lune insists.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: We ask people what they want before we change them. Revolutionary.

lines.speaker: PREFECT LYSANDER CRANE
lines.text: The Ascendancy stands at the door. Shields up. No cheating.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: Eighty years under the sea keeping a voice in a box. The Fracture's just the box getting bigger.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: The sea always wins, eventually. We make eventually take a very long time.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: The garage has proper pumps. I like a place with proper pumps.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: Surface air is very thin. Nobody warned me.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: Surface people. We don't get many. We don't want many.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: You got every pod out. Every one. I don't forget that.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: You and your lamp. Come down sometime. The palace is dry enough for socks.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: My grandmother would have liked you. She liked people who went back.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: The voice in the walls got louder nine days ago.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: The cult's gone quiet. Good.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: Somebody cut the eastern pumps. I want a name.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: A centimetre a minute. The city's breathing again.

lines.speaker: CHIEF ODA
lines.text: Thalassia's pumped out. I've seen three sunrises now. Still on fire.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: The Fracture was the best thing that ever happened to my business. I'm not proud. I'm rich.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: Everybody in this city is wearing something over something. The Fracture just made it obvious.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: The night market. Every secret in Neon passes through here eventually. Most of them stop to eat.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: My little room. Should I be flattered or should I be running?

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: The famous survivor. I've heard prices for you.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: You pay. You don't haggle. You're terrible at this.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: For you, the good secrets. Half price. Don't tell anyone I have a heart.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: If anyone ever asks me where you are, I'll sell them the wrong answer. Free.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: Silver hair, eyes like a bruise. Paid in Genesis credit.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: The ledger's gone. Everyone's very nervous. Business is wonderful.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: Bending coats asked first. They always ask first.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: Someone bought every map of the Shattered Expanse in the city. Twice.

lines.speaker: VESPER
lines.text: Neon City has a door now. I've already got people selling tickets.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The crash site landed on my crew's lunch break. Nobody hurt. The sandwiches did not make it.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The Fracture is a twelve-week cleanup job. We're on week thirty. I've stopped counting weeks.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The crash site. Hard hats past the tape. I don't care who you are; the tape doesn't either.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: Thirty years of building. First time I've been asked to un-build something that fell from the sky.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: Past the tape, you wear a hat. No hat, no past.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The operator. You keep off my scaffolding. I appreciate that.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: You're welcome on site any time. Hat's on the hook with your name on it.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: If I ever get a crew of people like you, I'll have this done in a week. Don't give me ideas.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: Vanguard wants the wreck's core by Friday. Friday was two Fridays ago.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The bastion sent engineers to help. Actual engineers. I nearly cried.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The plaza business kept my crew home a day. A day! Somebody owes me a day.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: They've reopened the lab under the bastion. My crew built the walls around that thing in the nineties. We never asked what it was.

lines.speaker: GLORIA HAYNES
lines.text: The crash site's clear. Clear. I'm taking a holiday. First one since the Fracture.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: Mid-race when it hit. The road bent. I made the corner anyway. That's the whole story and it's a good one.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: The Fracture made the avenue a track. Potholes, debris, purple light. Best course in the city.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: Meet's at midnight on the avenue. Nobody official. Everybody fast.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: This corner's where you line up. Don't line up unless you mean it.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: You drive? Prove it.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: You held your line at the meet. Most don't.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: You beat me once. Once. I think about it more than I should.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: You're the only one I'd give my car to. Don't crash it. I would know.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: Vanguard shut the midnight meet. We moved it. They haven't found it.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: A captain from the bastion came to the meet. Didn't shut it down. Watched. Fast eyes.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: The masks blocked the avenue at midnight. Cost us a race. Somebody's going to pay for that.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: Heard your voice-in-the-ear can see every camera on the loop. Tell it to look away at the finish.

lines.speaker: KAI TANAKA
lines.text: Avenue's open end to end. Clean. Fast. The meet's never been bigger.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: The casino lights went purple. The gamblers didn't look up. I've never respected them more.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: The Fracture's the only thing that's ever got past me on this door. Once.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Neon Crown Casino. The rope's the law. I'm the judge.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Casino Row. Everything's for sale, including the people selling it. Not me. I'm just the door.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Dress code's whatever I say it is. Tonight it's 'not you'.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: The operator. Weapon on the counter, you can go in. Weapon on your hip, you can go home.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: You're on the list. Permanently. Don't make me regret the ink.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Anybody gives you trouble inside, you find me. Then they find out why the rope's the law.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Syndicate's got a new boss and new rules. The rules change nightly. The boss doesn't.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: A Nexus captain came through Neon. Didn't gamble. Asked about Sable. Everyone asks about Sable.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Masks on the Row last night. Syndicate's idea of a party. I didn't let them in.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: Heard your companion's got a past the Syndicate wants to buy. Tell it the rope's the law.

lines.speaker: VEX MORALES
lines.text: The Row's calmer. Fewer fights at the door. I'm bored. I'm not complaining.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: The club's lights synced to the rift's hum the night it happened. They never un-synced. It's the best set we've ever had.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: The Fracture gave Neon its colour. Before that it was just neon.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Neon Afterglow. Guest list, best sound in the city, lights that follow the rift. You're on it. Obviously.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: The Nightlife quarter never sleeps. Neither do I. It's a problem.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Guest list? Hmm. Name?

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Oh you're the operator! Come in, come in, the floor's yours.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: You dance like someone who's been shot at. It works. Honestly it works.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: The booth's yours. The good one. Don't make me explain to the DJ.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Syndicate took over the door money. I'm pretending I didn't notice.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: A Nexus captain came in. In uniform. On a Friday. The floor cleared like a rift.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Masks on the Row! We did a masked night. Then the real masks came. Awkward.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Everyone's talking about your ghost. The voice. I want to put it on a flyer.

lines.speaker: HANA SATO
lines.text: Best month we've had. The lights still follow the rift. Softer now.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: Fixed an implant the week after that wasn't from any company on Earth. Or so I say. I say it a lot.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: The Fracture fried every screen in Neon. I've had a queue ever since.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: Tech-repair, Neon Mods. Cracked screen, fried implant, cursed drone — same price.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: This stall's held together with tape and spite. Like most of Neon.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: Broken something? No? Then you're in the way.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: You bring me weird parts. I like weird parts.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: You're the only customer who asks what I did instead of what it costs.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: That implant I don't talk about? I'll show you. Nobody else. Don't be weird about it.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: Syndicate's buying up every rift-touched part in Neon. I'm hiding mine.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: A Nexus captain's people bought thirty comms units. Paid full price. I didn't know how to react.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: The masks had cheap transmitters. Syndicate stock. I've got six on the bench.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: Pulled a log off a Syndicate relay. Your companion's name's in it. Older than the Fracture. I didn't say that.

lines.speaker: DEX OKORO
lines.text: The queue's shorter. The parts are cleaner. I'm almost out of excuses.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: The broth's been simmering since the Fracture. Never stopped. Neither have I.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: The night it hit I fed two hundred people for free. Some of them still come back and pay.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Noodle stall, Neon Metro. Twenty years. The broth's older than the metro.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Eat first. Whatever's chasing you can wait for noodles.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Sit. Eat. Then we see.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: You eat everything. Good. I don't trust people who leave broth.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: You're family now. Family eats first and pays later. Much later.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: If you ever need a place to be, this stall is it. Day or night. The broth's always on.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Syndicate came for protection money. I gave them noodles. They left.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: A captain from Nexus ate here. Two bowls. Said nothing. Tipped well.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: The masked crowd came past the metro. I shouted at them. They moved. Masks don't like noodles.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Someone says your companion was built in Nexus long ago. So was the metro. Both still work.

lines.speaker: LIN YUE
lines.text: Full stall every night. People talking, not whispering. That's the sound of a city.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: I was off duty in the casino. The lights went purple and every alarm went off at once. I worked that night anyway.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: The Fracture made Neon honest for one night. Then it was Neon again.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: Neon beat. Casino Row to the metro. Every door's got a bribe behind it and I don't take them.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: The Row at night's the most honest place in the city. Everyone's lying, so nobody's fooled.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: Weapon stays holstered on the Row. That's not advice.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: The operator. You've behaved. Keep behaving.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: You're the only armed stranger in Neon I don't follow. Take that as the compliment it is.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: If the Syndicate ever comes for you, I'll be there before they are. That's not in my job description.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: The Syndicate's got a new boss. The old one's 'retired'. Nobody's found him.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: Nexus sent a captain to coordinate. Straight as a rail. The Row doesn't know what to do with her.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: Masks on the Row. Syndicate stock. I've filed it. It'll go nowhere. I filed it anyway.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: The Syndicate's asking about your companion. Loudly. Watch your back on the Row.

lines.speaker: OFFICER RHEA BANKS
lines.text: Fewer calls. Fewer bodies. The Row's still the Row, but quieter.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: Twenty years in Neon. The Fracture's the only thing that ever surprised me. Took about a minute.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: The Fracture didn't change Neon. Neon was already broken. It just lit it better.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: This beat's a joke. The Row, the metro, the casino. Everybody's guilty; I just pick who's guilty today.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: I like the metro steps. Good view of everyone pretending not to see me.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: Keep walking.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: The operator. Not in my notebook yet. That's a good place to not be.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: You're all right. Neon doesn't do all right. Enjoy it.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: You're the only one in this city I'd call if it mattered. Don't tell Rhea; she thinks it's her.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: Syndicate's recruiting kids off the Row. I move them on. They come back.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: A Nexus captain's running joint patrols. Paperwork's doubled. Arrests have too. Fine.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: The masks were Syndicate. Everyone knows. Nobody says. I said. Nobody listened.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: Your companion's name's on a Syndicate buy list. Someone thinks it's worth money. Someone's going to try.

lines.speaker: OFFICER MARCO DIAZ
lines.text: A quiet Row. I've got nothing to do. I'm going to sit on the steps and hate it.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: I was in the undercity. The screens all showed the same face for a second. I've been trying to find it since.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: The Fracture rewrote the Neon grid. Somebody had to read it. It was me. I didn't want it to be.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: The undercity. Under the metro. Clean nodes, bad lighting, nobody looking. Perfect.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: Don't go past the third pillar. Not because of me. Because of what's past it.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: D-don't look at me. Look at the wall. Thanks.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: Oh. You. Okay. You're okay.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: I pulled your feed off the Syndicate's grid. They see nothing. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: You're the only one who knows where I sleep. That's… that's trust. Don't waste it.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: Syndicate's scanning the undercity for implants. I'm hiding. It's going well. It's not going well.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: Nexus sent a captain. Her people don't scan the undercity. I checked. Twice.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: The masks had Syndicate transmitters. I counted them. Four hundred. Someone paid for a crowd.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: I saw the lab logs. NOVA. Pre-Fracture. Built to find someone. I didn't tell anyone. Except you.

lines.speaker: JUNO PARK
lines.text: The grid's quiet. I came up for air. The sky's fine. I went back down. Baby steps.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The night the sky cracked, the house lost for the first time in thirty years. Rift-roulette. Someone won big and vanished.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The Fracture is the only thing I have ever seen beat the house. I do not intend to let it happen twice.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: Neon Crown. The floor is mine. Every table, every camera, every tell.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The house always wins. Lately the house has been nervous. The house does not get nervous.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The tables are for guests. Are you a guest?

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The operator. You do not gamble. I find that suspicious and admirable.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: You are welcome on my floor. Few are. Fewer deserve it.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The private room is yours whenever you need to not be seen. No questions. No charge. That is unheard of.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The Syndicate has new management. New management wants a percentage. I am negotiating.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: A Nexus captain toured the floor. She counted the exits. So do I.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: Masks on the Row. Syndicate theatre. I closed the floor for an hour. It cost me. It would have cost more.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: There is a buyer asking about your companion. The price is high. The buyer is not Syndicate. That worries me more.

lines.speaker: SILAS CRANE
lines.text: The floor is calm. The house wins again. I am almost disappointed.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Every car in the Neon garage started at once. Empty. I turned them off one by one. Took an hour. Loved it.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: The Fracture's the best thing that ever happened to tuning. Rift static does things to a turbo.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Neon Mods, the garage side. Dealer's next door. I'm the one who makes it go.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: This bay's mine. The one with the pink light. Don't ask about the pink light.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Need a tune? No? Then mind the hoist.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: The operator! Your ride's got a rattle. I can hear it from here.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: You're the only one who lets me do what I want to an engine. It shows.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: I built you something. It's in the back. Don't tell the dealer; it's not on any list.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Syndicate wants a cut of every tune. I've started doing them at night.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: A Nexus captain's people brought in six trucks. Fleet work! Steady money!

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: The masks blocked the garage for an hour. I tuned a car anyway. Nobody stops a tune.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Heard your ghost can see every camera on the loop. Ask it where the Syndicate parks.

lines.speaker: TASHA GREENE
lines.text: Garage is full, nobody's shooting, and I got the pink light fixed. Best week.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: I was on the metro when it hit. The train stopped. Then it kept going. Nobody was driving. I got off. Fast.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: The Fracture doubled my runs. Everyone wants everything now, and now's a bit later than it used to be.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Neon Metro's my hub. Every line, every exit, every shortcut nobody's supposed to know.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: The Row's quick money, the undercity's quiet money, the metro's where I breathe.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: You in my lane? You're in my lane.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Hey! The operator! You're fast, I've seen you.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: You and me, we're the fastest things in Neon that aren't on fire.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Best person on the Row. I'd race you for the title but I'd lose and I know it.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Syndicate's got runners on the Row. They're slow. They're armed. Slow and armed is a bad mix.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: A Nexus captain's people hired me for a run. Paid upfront. Who does that?

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: The masks slowed me down ten minutes. Ten! I went through the undercity.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Dex says your companion's in a Syndicate log. Dex says a lot. Dex is usually right.

lines.speaker: BENNY REYES
lines.text: Metro's running on time. On time! I've got nothing to complain about and it's weird.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: Every cabinet in the arcade played itself. All night. High scores everywhere. I kept them. Felt right.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: The Fracture gave Rift Runner its best level. It wasn't there before. Nobody coded it.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: The arcade, Casino Row. Tokens, cabinets, one machine that eats every third coin. It's a feature.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: High score on Rift Runner hasn't moved in a week. The name's 'NOVA'. Don't ask me.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: Tokens are a Nex each! No, you can't have a free one.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: Hey, the operator! You beat Rift Runner level three. Nobody beats three.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: You're the only one who plays the broken cabinets. I think they like you.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: I'll tell you the secret: the third-coin machine gives them back at midnight. Only to me. Now to you.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: Syndicate wants the arcade for a 'meeting room'. Over my high scores.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: A Nexus captain came in. Played one game. Won. Left. Terrifying.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: The masks came in for a photo. I charged them. Tokens, each. Nobody argued.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: The 'NOVA' high score just updated. It's higher. Nobody was at the cabinet.

lines.speaker: IVY CHEN
lines.text: Full arcade, every night. The broken cabinet fixed itself. I'm not asking.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: The sky's a screen, friend. The Fracture's a crack in the screen. I've said it for forty years. Now people listen.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: I saw the sky crack and I laughed. Not because it was funny. Because I was right.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: Casino Row. The loudest place in the world to say the quiet thing.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: I preach from the metro steps. The trains agree with me. Listen.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: Count the stars tonight. Then count them again.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: You again. You listen. Most walk. Listening's the first step.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: You've seen what's behind the screen. I can tell. We're the only two who have.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: When they switch the screen off, you'll be the one who notices. I'm glad. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: The Syndicate thinks it runs Neon. The screen runs Neon. The Syndicate's just a pop-up.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: A captain from the wall came through. Honest eyes. The screen doesn't like honest eyes.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: Masks! Faces on faces! The screen laughed. I heard it.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: The voice in your ear is older than the crack. I told you. I told everyone. Now you know.

lines.speaker: OLD MOSS
lines.text: The crack's closed. The screen's still a screen. Don't forget. Nobody else will remember.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The night the sky cracked, every camera in Neon went blind for nine seconds. I made more in those nine seconds than in the year before.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The Fracture is a market. Everything else is a rumour about the market.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: Casino Row. Every shortcut has an owner. You are standing on mine.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: Neon City. Twenty-two million cameras. Nine of them are mine. The rest can be rented.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: Every camera sees you. Every camera can lie. Tonight they are saying you are nobody.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: You won on the loop. The Syndicate wants your name. I have not sold it. Yet.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: Weapons, vehicles, secrets. For you, slightly less than everything. That is as generous as I get.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: Thinking like you do is expensive. I have decided to invest.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The Syndicate's new boss is buying rift-grade parts by the crate. Someone is building something.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: A Nexus captain is asking about me. I have told the cameras to show her a nice view of the harbor.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The masks were a count. Four hundred transmitters. Someone wanted to know how many of you there are.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The relay under the Aegis tower was pointed at your apartment eleven days before the Fracture. You already know. I just know who paid.

lines.speaker: FIXER SABLE
lines.text: The market is quiet. Prices are down. I find I do not mind. Do not tell anyone.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: I was airborne when the sky cracked. The instruments gave up. I did not. That is the whole of flying.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: The Fracture made the air routes unstable. I fly them anyway. Engineering, stubbornness, a little luck.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: Thalassia's air terminal. Seaplanes for the hops, a submersible for the deep. I fly the first and hum through the second.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: Thalassia sits deeper than most maps admit. The maps are being modest.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: That is not better news.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: We are crossing between continents. Strap in and say nothing clever.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: You jumped out of my aircraft once. I have forgiven you. I have not forgotten.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: I would fly you through the seam itself if you asked. Please do not ask.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: Currents are restless under the dome. The shadow in the lane has been seen twice this week.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: A Nexus captain is asking for flights to the Isles. I have told her the weather. The weather is me.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: The surface has masks in its plazas. The dome has kelp. I prefer the kelp.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: The archive says your companion was built before the first Fracture. The Archivist says it with respect. That is rare.

lines.speaker: PILOT NERI
lines.text: Clear skies between continents. I did not think I would say that again.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: I was at forty metres when it hit. The light went violet. I surfaced into a cracked sky. Best dive ever. Worst.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The Fracture made the deep sing. You can hear it through the hull. I like it. The others don't.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: Thalassia port, the diver's locker. Pressure seals, locked. Lights, violet past forty. Don't look up.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The dome's the only city where the ceiling's the ocean and nobody minds.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: Keep the seal locked till the chamber's clear. Please. For me.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The surface walker! You held the port while the dock cycled. I saw.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: You're the only surfacer who doesn't panic at violet. I've decided that means something.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: I'll take you to the deep lane. Where the shadow lives. Nobody else. Say the word.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The shadow in the lane's circling more. The Archivist says it's listening. To what?

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: Pilot Neri's running more flights to the surface. Something's coordinating up there.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: Surface news: masks in the Nexus plaza. Down here we just have fish. Prefer it.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The archive found a record with your companion's name. Pre-Fracture. The Archivist went quiet for a day.

lines.speaker: CORAL ADEYEMI
lines.text: The lane's calm. The shadow's gone deep. The dome's lights stopped flickering. I miss the singing a bit.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: The ferry was mid-crossing when it hit. The sea went still. Flat. Then it remembered. We made the dome.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: The Fracture is a tide. It goes out. It comes in. You learn the hours.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Ferry agent, Thalassia port. Next boat to the dome on the hour, weather permitting. Weather rarely permits.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Seasick bags are free. Use them. The crossing's honest about what it is.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Ticket? No? Then step back from the rail, love.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: The surfacer. You held the dock. The whole port talks about it.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: You're the only passenger who's never used a bag. I'm impressed and a little suspicious.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Front of the queue, every crossing. I've told the crew. Don't make me wave at you.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Crossings are down to two a day. The shadow in the lane's got the captains nervous.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: A Nexus captain booked passage. In writing. We don't get 'in writing' down here.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Surface news comes down slow. Masks in a plaza, they say. Sounds like a surface problem.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: The Archivist's been asking about your companion. Politely. She's always polite. It's unnerving.

lines.speaker: MAE OKONJO
lines.text: Four crossings a day again. Calm sea. The captains are bored. Good.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: The storm came the day the sky cracked and it never left. Out here that's just weather now.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: Sand gets into everything. The Fracture got into the sand. Work it out.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: Solara garage. Dune Gate's that way, the Ribcage past it. Don't go to the Ribcage.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: This is the only shade for twenty miles. I sell it by the hour. For you, the day.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: I can fix it. The bill might hurt more than the crash.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: You won the convoy run in a storm, in that. I'm still annoyed about it.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: More than you have, usually. For you, we negotiate. Don't tell the racers.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: There's a car in the back bay. It's yours. I built it. Don't say anything; the front end's listening.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: Raiders hit a convoy past the mesas. The storm got them first. The storm's on nobody's side.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: A Nexus captain wants trucks that'll cross the dunes. I told her the trucks are fine. The drivers aren't.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: News from the cities: masks, crowds, politics. Out here the sand doesn't care what you wear.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: Vyrak's been circling the garage. It knows something about your companion. It won't say. Dragons.

lines.speaker: MECHANIC ROOK
lines.text: Storm's calmer. Convoys are through. I've got time to fix my own truck. First time in a year.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: The caravan was three days out when the sky cracked. We saw it from the dunes. We kept walking. What else?

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: The Fracture made water the only currency. I sell water. Draw your own conclusions.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Solara terminal, the trader's row. Water first, stories second, everything else third.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Shade costs extra. Everything costs extra. This is the desert.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Water's two Nex. Stories are free. Pick one.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: The convoy winner! Rook's still complaining. It's wonderful.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: You're the only customer who pays for shade. I've started giving it free. Don't tell.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Family rate. Water, shade, the good dates. You've earned the dates.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: The caravan's late. Sandstorm or raiders. Either way, prices go up.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: A Nexus captain's buying water by the truck. For a district. I asked which. She said 'mine'.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Cities have masks. Deserts have sand. The sand's more honest.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Vyrak says your companion is old. Dragons don't say old lightly.

lines.speaker: ZAHRA HADDAD
lines.text: Caravans on time. Water's cheaper. I'm making less. I don't mind. Write that down; it won't last.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: Every panel on the array lit up purple. Fed the grid at ten times rating. For a minute. Then they sulked for a week.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The Fracture made the sun louder. The arrays hear it. I clean them at dawn so they can listen.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The solar fields. Every panel feeds the city; every grain of sand fights it. I'm the referee.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: We clean the arrays at dawn. You're welcome to help. It's beautiful. It's also miserable.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: Mind the cables. Mind the panels. Mind everything, actually.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The operator! You cleaned a panel once. Badly. I was touched.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The arrays like you. I don't know how I know. They sing a bit when you're near.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: Dawn tomorrow, the north array. I'll show you what the sun sounds like. Nobody else gets that.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: Raiders cut the east cable. Again. I fixed it. Again. We're in a rhythm.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: A Nexus captain wants panels for the bastion. I sent forty. She sent a thank-you. Nobody sends those.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The cities have their crowds. The arrays have the sun. I know which I'd rather read.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: The arrays sang when the Nexus lab opened. Across the whole continent. Your companion's in that song.

lines.speaker: IDRIS BELLO
lines.text: Full output, no storms, clean arrays. The sun's singing in tune.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: The glacier moved the day the sky cracked. Glaciers do not move in a day. This one did.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: The storm does not kill you quickly. It convinces you to stop moving. The Fracture taught it that.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: Frostveil, the lower camp. The glacier's up. The caverns are in. The summit's for people who've stopped listening.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: Check your heat pack before your weapon. Every time. The cold doesn't care about your aim.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: Whoever sent you should be careful.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: You climbed to the caverns in my prints. Every one. Good.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: That answer is why I agreed to guide you. I don't guide twice.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
lines.text: The crew we pulled out of the crown. Nine people. They ask about you. I tell them you'll come.

lines.speaker: RANGER KEST
